why: Owner, 2026-10-30, after trying the Midnight Gallery and Neon Vault rooms: the code-drawn rooms look like low-quality 3D and run poorly on a phone; instead an image AI makes the art for each theme's room (the 'third place', away from the collection), and the app lays its own live light, particles, depth and sound over it. This is the pilot for two themes; the other themes follow once these are judged.
instructions: Any image AI: follow the Drive doc 'ART_START_HERE (any AI: images + video)'. Claim it with {request id}.CLAIMED-{model}.txt first. takes 2 = make 2 versions named _take1/_take2 before the extension. One image at a time; stop at the first failure or credit warning and say how far you got. Save to 'Titan Reliquary/art-incoming (AI images + video)/artreq_20261030-1500_room-plates-pilot-afterhours-neon/' with the exact file names at full native resolution, then write artreq_20261030-1500_room-plates-pilot-afterhours-neon.DONE.txt next to this request (one line per file: ok or skipped: reason; your model name and date).

deliverable_spec.wide: 21:9 (or the widest your model makes), at least 3440x1472, PNG: the room is panned across with a finger on a phone and seen whole on a desktop
deliverable_spec.portrait: 9:16, at least 1440x2560, PNG: the same place from the same spot, composed for a phone held upright
deliverable_spec.depth: OPTIONAL, only if your tool can derive it from the image you just made (for example an image-editing model asked for a depth map of it): a greyscale depth map of the wide take, same size and framing, white = near, black = far, smooth, no text. Skip it otherwise and say so in the DONE file; never guess one by hand.
deliverable_spec.consistency: wide and portrait are the same place, light and time of night, so the app can switch between them when the phone turns

global_style: Real photography, not a render: shot on a full-frame camera with a 24-35 mm lens at night, true reflections, physically accurate materials, deep blacks with detail, practical light sources only, soft volumetric light, rich natural grading, fine film grain. Calm, expensive, cinematic. It must not look like a video game or a 3D render.
negative: no readable text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no signage with words, no watermark, no frame, no people, no faces, no hands, no coins, no 3D-render plastic look, no oversaturation, no HDR halos, no fisheye

Seen at eye level from where you would stand in it, as a place to be in (no coins, no collection, no display cases in front).
